newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end weaker, underperform on soft dlr.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end weaker, underperform on soft dlr.

text.p: Canadian bonds ended weaker on Wednesday, underperforming U.S. treasuries as a sharp drop in the value of the Canadian dollar pulled prices lower, analysts said.

"We got a little bit of drag down by the currency here. The currency took a noticeable sharp turn for the worse and I think that's affected our market," said Michael Gregory, a fixed-income economist and strategist with Lehman Brothers Canada Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.20 to C$115.89 to yield 6.755 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 14/32 to yield 6.69 percent. The spread between the bonds widened to seven basis points from two basis points at Tuesday's close.
Canadian bonds weakened as the currency broke through technical support at the C$1.3885 (US$0.7202) level to close much weaker.

"The currency weakened dramatically and Canada-U.S. spreads have widened dramatically," said one bond trader with a Canadian bank. "A lot of people have argued for a while that Canada was a bit overdone and today there seems to be the first crack in the armor."
The trader said he had seen only light flows and thought selling was likely U.S. driven.
In new issue news, the Province of New Brunswick on Wednesday issued C$250 million of 6.75 percent bonds due June 27, 2017 in financial markets.
The bond was priced at 99.339 to yield 6.811 percent, 20 basis points over the Government of Canada yield curve.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.15 to C$107.77 to yield 6.190 percent, while the U.S. 10-year traded rose 8/32 to yield 6.40 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 21 basis points from 26 basis points at Tuesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.84 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.07 percent.
